newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures tumbled to their lowest level for two weeks on Friday after a slew of economic reports revived fears of U.S. interest rate rises while a fragile mark unsettled European interest rate futures.

Traders said the tone of the French market next week would depend very much on how the U.S. bond market ended the session and whether investors believed mark weakness would spur the Bundesbank to raise interest rates.

The September bond future tumbled as low as 130.06, its lowest level since July 16, and settled at 130.20, down 0.66 centimes. Benchmark 10-year bond yields climbed as high as 5.53 percent from 5.44 percent on Thursday.

The selloff was sparked by a stronger-than-expected rise in a long-awaited U.S. July jobs report and then exacerbated by an unexpectedly strong increase in the price component of a U.S. purchasing managers survey.
Analysts said the figures did not augur well for the coming week and speculation about the possibility of tighter German monetary policy could also weigh.
"Clearly from the markets point of view the main issue is where does the mark go next," Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said.

He said it was a tough call whether the Bundesbank would put up rates to stem the mark's decline and prevent domestic price rises but in the near term the risk was that European yield curves would flatten further.

Valerie Plagnol, economist at CCF said "The main question is whether the Bundesbank can, or will, initiate something alone. I think it can only move if it is perceived as a coordinated action. If not they're taking too much risk of being contradicted by the markets."

Speculation the German central bank could move has been bubbling since last week when it fixed its key repo rate for two weeks, until next Thursday, rather than the usual four weeks during the summer break.
September PIBOR fell four basis points, leaving implied three-month interest rates at 3.53 percent, compared with cash rates of 3.35 percent late on Friday.
The franc was relatively stable at 3.3715 per mark.
